findings.claim: No real-browser test drives a wheel over a `.loft` provider player, so the I7 forwarding for the iframe case is unchecked. That case is the path through the GestureOverlay in the parent document while the overlay is interactive.
findings.impact: A regression that left the overlay pointer-events none outside ads and end screens would pass every suite. A wheel over a YouTube `.loft` would then stop scrolling the canvas, which is the defect r7's V-1 described.
findings.evidence: PlayerLayer.tsx:240-261 forwards only wheels that reach the layer frame in the parent document. GestureOverlay.tsx:45-46 covers the frame `absolute inset-0` with `pointerEvents: interactive ? "auto" : "none"`, so the wheel reaches the frame only while the overlay is interactive. The I7 cases (player-layer-desktop.spec.ts, the 'a wheel that starts on the player' case; player-layer-wheel*.spec.ts) all use openFilePage, which opens video0000001, a native video.
findings.repro: Mutation: in GestureOverlay.tsx:46, force `pointerEvents: "none"` for `.loft` players. No I7 case fails, because none of them opens a `.loft` file.

bucket_proposal.reason: This is a test gap. Under the revised I7, the code path (the overlay in the parent document takes the wheel and the frame forwards it) satisfies the invariant by reading.

findings.proposed_fix: Add an I7 case on a `.loft` fixture with a stub provider iframe: wheel over the frame while the overlay is interactive, and check that the canvas scrolls by the same amount as a wheel beside the player.

findings.claim: Still open from r7: the wheel forwarder drops the horizontal part of a mostly-vertical wheel. It calls preventDefault and applies only deltaY to the slot's scroller.
findings.impact: A diagonal trackpad scroll over the player loses its sideways part. No file-page scroller is known to scroll sideways, so nothing visible is expected.
findings.evidence: PlayerLayer.tsx:247 returns only when |deltaX| > |deltaY|. PlayerLayer.tsx:252-259 then calls preventDefault and does `scroller.scrollTop += event.deltaY * unit`. Nothing applies deltaX.

bucket_proposal.reason: I7 is about the vertical amount on a scroller that only scrolls vertically, and no user path is known.

specification_compliance: The commit under review (ee4e6f6e) records review r7 and the owner's revision of I7. It changes no product code. The list of fix commits since r7 says '(none)'.

r7 V-1 (a wheel over a provider iframe is not forwarded) is now judged against the revised I7. The revision exempts the moments when a provider iframe takes the pointer itself (an ad, the end screen, YouTube UI mode). Otherwise GestureOverlay (GestureOverlay.tsx:45-46, `absolute inset-0`, pointer-events auto while interactive) sits in the parent document over the iframe. The wheel lands on it, bubbles to the layer frame's listener (PlayerLayer.tsx:261) and is forwarded to the slot's nearest scroller. Exactly when the overlay is non-interactive, the wheel goes into the iframe, which the revision accepts. By reading, the code satisfies revised I7. No browser test confirms it (T-2).
r6 B-1 stays fixed: PlayerLayerProvider always returns PlayerLayerContext.Provider (PlayerLayer.tsx:305-310), and only PlayerLayerFrame is conditional.
r6 B-2 stays fixed: onWheel leaves ctrl+wheel, mostly-horizontal wheels, full screen and inner scrollers that can still scroll to the browser (PlayerLayer.tsx:245-251).

I1, I2, I3, I5, I8, I9, I12 and I13: no code changed since r7, and the mechanisms read as before. They are a layout effect after every commit, ResizeObservers on the slot and its ancestors, capturing scroll, rAF following of transitions, display none plus inert while the slot has no box, the in-place fallback without a store, an error boundary keyed per served id, and a single served slot.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: Wheel scrolling over the player is applied by hand as an instant scrollTop change, so it ignores the browser's smooth wheel scrolling and overscroll-behavior that a wheel beside the player gets.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: A wheel over the video moves the canvas in steps rather than with the smooth animation the same wheel gets beside the player.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A player element that handles the wheel in script without CSS overflow (none known today, a future slider or an addon embed) loses the wheel to the page, because innerScrollerTakes only looks at overflow-y auto or scroll.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: It applies only if such an element is added; the user would see the page scroll instead of the control reacting.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A diagonal trackpad scroll over the player loses its horizontal component.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: It is visible only if the slot's scroller also scrolled horizontally, which is not known on the file page.

regression_risks: The forwarding over a `.loft` relies on GestureOverlay staying interactive and covering the iframe outside ads and end screens. A change to that gating silently breaks I7 for `.loft`, and no test catches it (T-2).

In the iOS shell, the store is created during the hydration commit and dropped on the post-hydration re-render. A player that renders in that first commit would mount in the layer once and then move into the slot.
Each new player element that scrolls or takes a wheel needs its own early return in onWheel, or the page takes the wheel from it.
test_coverage: I7: a native-video vertical wheel (desktop), ctrl+wheel (synthetic, desktop), the settings panel taking the wheel and then chaining at its end (390x200), and pseudo full screen (390x844) are covered. No case covers a `.loft` provider player, or the non-interactive overlay moments that the revision exempts.
I12 and I13 are covered in jsdom only; the I9 fallback has a jsdom unit test.
The rest is as in r7: I2 has no case for the sheet at each snap, and I4 has none for many of the surfaces it lists.
not_verified: I ran no test and no browser; every claim was reasoned from the code.

Whether the YouTube iframe in LoftPlayer is actually rendered under GestureOverlay in every `.loft` mode (Vimeo embed, link card, restricted card). I checked GestureOverlay and its single use in MediaControlsContainer only.
Whether the content of commit ee4e6f6e is limited to docs. I relied on the prompt's statement that there are no fix commits and on the commit subject.
Safari/WebKit wheel delivery over a fixed layer.
trajectory: No fix round since r7: the one new commit (ee4e6f6e) records r7 and revises the I7 invariant text, with no code change. The r7 trajectory still holds. Round 1 (5fc0b20) removed a branch, the Fragment return. Round 2 (6dc5eae) added four early-return branches to onWheel on top of the earlier 'no scroller' branch, so the hand-made scroll chaining has been patched more than once. This round settles V-1 by narrowing the invariant to what the design can do, not by adding another branch. The wheel-forwarding design is still patched: it was extended once and then its specification was relaxed.
